correctness.rationale: For all n>=2, the Cartan matrix has determinant n+1 and its image equals the kernel of the weighted-sum congruence modulo n+1. This is precisely the claimed invariant semigroup. Every nontrivial subgroup has fixed subspace of codimension at least two; prime-order fixed spaces give all and only irreducible singular components. Their generic stabilizers and character multiplicities follow by complete residue counting. Primitive coordinate rays give class group Z/(n+1) and canonical index by the sum of weights. Ambro's strictly-interior formula gives mld_o=n/2 after adding one to every zero fractional coordinate; the closed-cone ages give the canonical/terminal threshold. The standard-library checker passed 45520 exact checks but is not substituted for the infinite argument.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2010 and 2015 Lipman-toric papers construct semigroups, quotient descriptions, Hilbert bases and Groebner generators, but their relevant sections do not give the consecutive-weight quotient identification together with the all-n prime-indexed singular components, generic transverse representations, and exact mld and canonical-index formulas. General cyclic-quotient smoothness and Ambro's toric discrepancy theorem imply corresponding criteria, and are explicitly credited; the present result computes their simultaneous consequences for a specific geometric semigroup family. This leaves residual uncertainty about unindexed specializations and the inaccessible 2007 weighted-graph full text.

value.rationale: This natural complete singularity classification connects geometric components and their dimensions to the distinct prime factors of the Cartan determinant. The simultaneous generic transverse quotient classification, closed-point discrepancy, canonical index and terminality give a sharp birational profile of the Lipman toric family, answering meaningful geometric questions not addressed by the source papers' Gröbner computations. Its importance rests on the full-family structural partition and explicit local invariants, not on numerical sampling or a cosmetic reformulation.
